miniProject.title: Operate and evolve a governed data path
miniProject.brief: Extend `loglab` with the security, recovery and governance records needed to operate its data path. Reuse the stream and transaction fixtures on your machine, proving policy and restore correctness before running a measured incident campaign.
steps: Threat-model `loglab` boundaries in `ops/`; implement mTLS or a faithful verifier for validity, matching trust-domain bundles and allowed SPIFFE IDs. During rotation, test unknown domains, expired SVIDs and unauthorized IDs against an independent policy table; retain overlapping-key tenant tests across retry, cache, migration and restore.

Persist redacted audit events in a tamper-evident chain; test edits, deletion, truncation and restore against an independently retained checkpoint. Add bounded-cardinality W3C-context telemetry and windowed SLOs; inject an incident with skewed display timestamps, retaining causal reconstruction against the fault schedule and marking unestablished order.

Record classification, retention, residency, transfer rules and deletion mechanisms per tier. Check deletion-ledger and cache-watermark propagation against a lineage inventory, including fresh-version resurrection attempts; retain fixed-snapshot backfill agreement and hand-oracle feature joins covering TTL, created timestamps and logged online-versus-offline equivalence under matching materialization state.

Build immutable retrieval-index generations from content-identified datasets and per-partition frontiers; check counts and deletions against a full-scan reference. Retain before-and-after publication crash tests and retained-generation rollback; add checksum-gated artifact serving, registry alias promotion and rollback with immutable producing-run lineage.

Apply sticky routing and expand-migrate-contract evolution to existing `proto/` and `storage/` data. Check mixed-version reads and writes, reconciled representations, readiness, drain and availability limits against a compatibility matrix; retain rollback tests and mark the irreversible boundary and roll-forward recovery path.

Restore base backup and archived WAL in isolation; check committed data, tenancy and current deletion policy against the ledger. After deterministic checks, drill fenced failover/failback; retain divergent tails, both fork points, acknowledged-write loss and detection, decision, restore, verification and switch timings.

Model foreground, replication fan-out, backup, restore and repair costs with concurrent recovery reserves. Queue-oracle tests check bounded admission, retry budgets, breakers and bulkheads before repeated open-loop chaos campaigns including backup/restore; retain trigger/abort cards, node-loss bottleneck comparisons, versions, workloads, SLOs, backlog, capacity, recovery and migration costs.
deliverables: The `ops/` security and governance layer with independent policy, audit, deletion, feature and artifact reference checks.
Verified backup, failover, failback and mixed-version migration runbooks with rollback boundaries and retained fault histories.
A production dossier with causal incident reconstruction, resource reservations, repeated campaign records and evidence-labeled cost and recovery claims.

rubric.pass: Your policy-table tests reject invalid or unauthorized identities during rotation and prevent cross-tenant access on normal, retry, cache, migration and restore paths with overlapping keys.
rubric.strong: Negative controls remove endpoint or storage enforcement independently; remaining defenses and audit records demonstrate the exact residual protection and key-compromise scope.

rubric.pass: Your lineage inventory, hand join and full-scan reference check deletion, deterministic backfills, feature equivalence and index counts. Publication crashes, alias rollback and artifact corruption have retained tests.
rubric.strong: A stale source republishes erased data with a fresh version and is rejected; rollback and restore preserve current deletion policy without rewriting immutable artifact lineage.

rubric.pass: Your ledger verifies isolated backup restore and both fenced promotions. Forks, divergent tails, acknowledged-write loss and recovery stages are recorded; mixed-version tests check rollback before the declared irreversible boundary.
rubric.strong: Broken archive continuity and an incomplete migration trigger explicit refusal or roll-forward recovery, with regression histories showing why a nominally successful job was insufficient.

rubric.pass: Your audit verifier detects tampering against an external checkpoint. Queue-model checks precede repeated campaigns; causal incident evidence, capacity predictions, recovery reservations and measured cost ledgers retain setup and uncertainty.
rubric.strong: The dossier distinguishes incident trigger from sustaining retry load, measures observer overhead, and explains a mistaken bottleneck prediction or losing policy without hiding the raw records.

miniProject.feedsInto: Policy checks, verified recovery, migration boundaries, lineage, artifact generations and incident evidence feed the formal extension's compatibility and reproduction tests and the capstone production dossier.
